summary: --fills leg 1 is a CONTAINMENT test and a containment test passes for free if its mask is large, so the mask was measured and moved rather than trusted. The leg-1 mask is 18,726 px, 6.10% of the frame (loop footprint 12,559, label 6,182); the five filled blocks' own footprint is 52,858 px, FOUR TIMES larger, so the lane's own mutant is the harder direction and not the easier one. Two mutants that are not the lane's: translating the loop footprint in x by 2/4/8/16/32/64 px leaves 100/368/890/1886/3774/7335 px outside and fails leg 1 on every one; rebuilding the footprint at w = 0/1/8/16/24/32/48 leaves 11962/8551/4445/2386/952/0/0 px outside, so w = 32 is the SMALLEST width at which the leg passes at all.
scenario: The scenario a new instrument's clean result invites -- a zero that could not have come out otherwise -- does not apply here. A two-pixel shift of the mask already breaks leg 1, and the width sweep says the goldens put their LINE_WIDTH dependence not merely somewhere inside the loop's region but at the loop's POSITION and at the suite's OWN WIDTH. That is a stronger statement than --fills prints, and it is what licenses reading the four moved device pixels as the cap clip working on a wide line loop in a capture named Fill.
evidence: docs/testing/line_cap_phase.py fills() legs 1 and 2, shader_mask(); docs/testing/line_priority.py BLOCKS/EDGES/our_edges()/text_mask(); goldens/results/Line_width/Fill_0000.0.png, Fill_0001.0.png, Fill_0032.0.png. Every number now committed to permanent source re-measures exactly: (271,93) master 51,155,151 / pre-deadband 51,154,152 / deadbanded 51,155,151 / golden 51,154,152, and (264,123) master 51,228,78 / pre-deadband 51,227,79 / deadbanded 51,228,78 / golden 51,227,79. summary: NOTES.md:355-361 carries the original 'nothing in this lane's diff can reach it' paragraph and NOTES.md:363-375 marks it WRONG, corrected in place by audit finding N4, directly underneath. The PR body carries the same paragraph in its 'Pass-2 audit remediated' section and was NOT given the same marker: it still reads 'and nothing in this branch's diff can reach it: with widen_lines false the generator emits the byte-identical fill shader it emitted before'. The body does correct it about 1,400 words later in the pass-2c section, so this is a currency defect rather than a contradiction left standing unremarked -- but it is the one place the lane applied its own standard unevenly, and the PR body is what the board and the next lane read first.
scenario: A reader scanning the body for 'Fill', which is what anyone re-opening this question does, hits the pass-2 section first, reads that the diff cannot reach Line_width/Fill_*, and re-derives the error that cost this lane an arm. This campaign's standing lesson is the same shape: a withdrawal appended at the end leaves the earlier assertion still asserting itself.
remediation: Two sentences in the PR body mirroring the NOTES.md block, at the paragraph that makes the claim. `gh pr edit --body-file` is broken on this host (Projects-classic GraphQL error) -- use the REST PATCH and read the value back. Worth doing before the fold; not worth holding it.
evidence: PR #141 body, 'One thing this lane cannot settle' in the 'Pass-2 audit remediated, and the device FAIL it found' section; docs/lanes/linecap13/NOTES.md:353-375.

summary: LEG C4 enumerates what its absolute can catch -- 'a capture that is not deterministic after all, a pair that is not the pair this file names, or a change that reaches this shader without anyone noticing' -- and justifies 26717 as 'the value the device measured twice with band 0 on this same binary'. True, and it omits that 'the device' was the THOR while the arm now judging it is on the NOVA. Every request in the chain carries "device": "" and nothing pins the pair-to-pair choice: arm 1 ran nova, arm 2 (which measured 26,717) ran thor, and arm 3's base is running on the nova per dispatch/running/*.owner. The same omission sits under N5's two-pixel measurement, which compares a nova capture with a thor one.
scenario: As written the reasoning transfers an absolute across an axis it does not name -- the shape AGENTS.md records as an availability change silently redefining a registered comparison. Had the two devices disagreed on this suite, C4 would have failed on the next arm and the regressed label would have stayed for a reason having nothing to do with the cap rule, with the prediction's own text offering no way to see it. MEASURED INSTEAD OF FLAGGED, on the one binary both devices have now run (apk_sha 215d41ca8268, disc 2-suites:00a36f5b): 166 of 166 captures byte-identical between the nova and the thor, Line_width 61 of 61 and Blend_tests 105 of 105. So the absolute is a fact about the binary and not about the thor, the must_not_move globs cannot fire on a device difference either, and the leg is right as registered.
remediation: Record the control, do not change the leg: one sentence in the prediction and in NOTES.md saying 26,717 was measured on the thor, that the judging pair may run on either handheld, and that the two are byte-identical on all 166 captures of this disc at one APK. This is worth more than this lane -- it is the first cross-device byte control on a multi-suite disc in this campaign, and AGENTS.md's 'Do not reach for the equivalence check to rescue it' paragraph, which records that the 62-of-62 equivalence has never been run on a large disc, is where it belongs.
